+from rich.console import Console
+from rich.text import Text
+
+console = Console(force_terminal=True)
+text = Text("Line 1\nLine 2", end="\n")
+# We want to see if there's a superfluous space or newline.
+# Let's capture the output.
+from io import StringIO
+console.file = StringIO()
+console.print(text)
+output = console.file.getvalue()
+print(f"Output: {repr(output)}")
+
+# Expected: "Line 1\nLine 2\n"
+# If bug exists: "Line 1\n\nLine 2\n\n" or something like that.
+# Actually, if Text.render adds 'end' after each line:
+# Line 1
+# \n (from join)
+# Line 2
+# \n (from end)
+# Wait, if Text.render is called on all_lines:
+# all_lines is "Line 1\nLine 2"
+# Text.render(all_lines) will:
+# 1. split "Line 1\nLine 2" into ["Line 1", "Line 2"]
+# 2. render "Line 1"
+# 3. yield end ("\n")
+# 4. render "Line 2"
+# 5. yield end ("\n")
+# Result: "Line 1\n\nLine 2\n"
+# But Console.print(text) also adds end if text is not a Text object? 
+# No, if it's a Text object, it uses __rich_console__.
+# And __rich_console__ calls all_lines.render(console, end=self.end).
+# So if self.end is "\n", we get "Line 1\n\nLine 2\n".
+# But the expected output for print(Text("Line 1\nLine 2")) is "Line 1\nLine 2\n".
